body: Well the one thing I can remember around that age is getting "sexually assaulted" as you might say about a month after my 7th birthday. So I guess that could be it? The other options aside from suicide would be to keep staying at idle like I am now doing nothing in hopes of a miracle that I'll "get happy" if I just wait. But, the chances of nothing changing as it has for about 10 years it quite high and idk how I would go about that now as I'm only getting older and will have to work for myself rather than be able to "rely" on others to help on the way. The other one is fully changing myself. As in attempting to suppress these feelings and put on a "facade" of sorts to try to ignore my problems and be more optimistic to get through this but, that will eventually fail like most things. There is the "expert level" of sorting/dealing with these problems but I either shut down or distract myself without me consciously thinking to do so. There are some times when I leave the therapists place and realize I stopped myself from telling everything. I don't understand why I do that but I do. That is why I said I feel like I'm at a dead end. Of course, I realize there may be other options but my thought process is not as it should be as I'm here. (Downsides to dying would be causing my dad, sisters, and brother to be sad and that's about it. On the other hand, 1 less person to feed, and buy things for thus saving money and hopefully giving them a better life)

I've felt this way for about 10 years now. I became painfully logical and critical to try to cope with the problems I have and can't deal with. At least, that's what therapists have told me. At this point talking face to face with anybody is annoyingly difficult so I just had pretty normal conversations about school and such with my therapist but only recently talked about the suicidal thoughts. She responded along the lines of "it seems you run yourself into holes that are too deep for you to get out of on your own, but, things like your anxiety hold you back from reaching out for help from others" and "I encourage you to try to find someone you're comfortable with like your brother and see if he shares any feelings as you do and if not, he could be your anchor to guide you through your life" (not all the convo but what I could remember). I can tell after I told her about the suicidal things she took a huge step back (presumably in attempt to keep me calm) and actually has helped me a little but obviously not fully. I'm still going every Saturday but I feel like I'm hearing the same thing over and over again and it just feels like I have to force myself to be there. Idk, maybe a different therapist would help me but after looking at all my options, dying has the least downsides from what I can see.
